Chess with Hamster. 2014 Video with Animation 2:40 Minute.

The chess game board become a place for re inventing and questioning the game limitation while, the Idea of playing the game and fredom of movement was accompanied by previouse rule re inforcing the monarchy system when you palay the game you are intering to a system that builds boundaries around the players thinking to addopt the Idea that there is a king that every one have to sacrifice himself in order to win the game.. but this vide will start playing around how to challenge these rules .

play your own chess, 2023

the work invited audiences to invent their own game with dialogues build between participant and many new games invented and become part of the animation shown beside the game. this version was part of the exhibition 

Chesign. 2023

In a workshop for the students of (Design Academy Iraq) I invited students to reinvent their new games in a way that reflects their vision for the world. The workshop lasted one week, and participants began building completely new games based on the issues they chose.

2005 The First Board

The idea of the board started in 2005 when Freedom Park was new especially Freedom Corner, which was claimed to be a free spot where everyone could speak at the time I wanted to work on it, and show it in the new game in Freedom Corner.

items.content_html:
May flames pave the way for You.

 

New National Museum in GdańskNew Art Museum part of National Museum in Gdańsk. 23.10.2021 - 27.02.2022

Kurdish art has been developing in complex political and economic conditions. Towards the end of the Iranian-Iraqi war (1980–1988), which claimed many victims on both sides of the conflict, the Kurdish people in Iraq experienced the horror of a genocide ordered by Saddam Hussain. The dramatic struggle for independence became the key element of the Kurdish culture and the policy of remembrance and constitutes not only a part of the collective experience, but also the dominating narration, through which the identity of the autonomous Region of Kurdistan is created. The development of a new language of art in a country struggling with wars and doomed to a fight for survival is particularly difficult. Nevertheless, a group of artists whose works are related to the reality that affects them have managed to accomplish it.

The works presented at the exhibition undertake the subject of the experience of the history, as well as social and lifestyle-related changes taking place in the region. Their authors belong to the generation of thirty- and forty-year olds and most of them have had an opportunity to study abroad, mainly in Germany, Great Britain and Scandinavia. Some of them returned to their homeland and have been teaching in schools of art, while others remained in the diaspora. The artists invited to the National Museum include: Hiwa K (Berlin/Sulaymaniyah), Sherko Abbas (Manchester), Kani Kamil (Manchester), Shirwan Fatih (Sulaymaniyah), Rebeen Hamarafiq (Sulaymaniyah), Rozhgar Mustafa (Sulaymaniyah), Sakar Sleman (Sulaymaniyah), Walid Siti (London), and Halgurd A. Baram (Sulaymaniyah).



Exhibition partner: GALLERY ARSENAŁ in Białystok

items.content_html:
Those People Working..

Currator: Avan Omar

This project has several virtues, view with solo and group art shows, seminars, discourse and text at different times and places. Avan Omer is an organiser and curator of this project and analyses its targets for this project.
As it is common sense these days in all venues, society, community and sectors after first integration or exposure with the other lots of questions will be generated after identifying yourself the following question is what's your occupation? Generally, we can point to the existence or the human that is connected to their job and became the title of that person sometimes.


Some people are distinguished by their occupation and became their surname. The value of this idea is getting approach and analyse it. There is a huge differ- ence between excitement and enthusiasm to be on board for this matter. Another headline of this concept is the gender has a role to divide the occupations, de- pending on its heavy duties or appropriations’. Ironically, the occupation depict- ing your value in society. This is always a sort of classification that came through or we can say labialization. We are coming to the point to describe the job what is the job?

What are the pros and cons? Is the economy having its affection on the equality and equity between the gender? How could we cope without having an occupa- tion?

This project highlights our integration with the jobs, activities, and connections. How this relates to the individuals? Aiming to sum up the verity of perspectives and unify them to see the outcome. Different discourses regarding gender with a bunch of groups that attended. Hence, this effort was run voluntarily and cooper- ated, did not have a fund or support by any organization or government. Mainly the performance was in Sulaymaniyah but, at different times and places. The fol- lowing step is arranging some seminars for that purpose.


Dropping
Art Show
By Rebeen Majed
On June 10th, 2021
At Esta Gallery2 in the Culture Factory of Sulaimany
Curator: Avan Omar

The theme of torture often appears in the works of Kurdish artists, which has an obvious connection with the history of their nation and the painful experiences of their families and friends.
Drops of milk fall at regular intervals onto the naked head of the artist filmed against a black background. Within a few minutes a small puddle of milk is formed on the top of the artist’s skull, and a thin trickle runs down his weary face. What we see is an obvious reference to the so- called Chinese water torture, in which cold water is slowly dripped onto the victim’s head. Seemingly mild and “humane”, deprived of spectacular violence and blood-shed, it is in reality painful, mentally debilitating and considered one of the most effective.
The theme of torture often appears in the works of Kurdish artists, which has an obvious connection with the history of their nation and the painful experiences of their families and friends.
The motif of dripping milk also refers to Rebeen’s experience of fatherhood. The artist looked after his newborn daughter while his wife was working toward her university degree. Attempting to cope with a new situation, weary with the day-to-day monotony and challenges, the artist was also haunted by fear for his daughter’s future, his desire to protect his daughter from experienced by Kurdish women sense of being unable to break through limiting social, religious and cultural circumstances.

backpacker-sitting-on-wall-and-looking-down-on-town

Rebeen Majid An artist and curator based in Sulaimany, South Kurdistan. Graduated from several places for his studies such as the Institute of fine art, the university for his bachelor and masters at the famous Goldsmith University, London. His work contains many different mediums and materials, fluctuating between concepts and displaying his outcomes in a contemporary vision. As well as, Rebeen had arranged and conducted many projects inside the Kurdish region and oversees.

items.title: Galeria Arsenal
items.summary: The title of the exhibition – May Flames Pave the Way for You – references the case of artists burning paintings in the…
items.content_html:
The title of the exhibition – May Flames Pave the Way for You – references the case of artists burning paintings in the streets of the Iraqi city of Sulaymaniyah* in the 1990s, a time when many artists of the older generation had already left the country while the younger generation sensed a depletion in the formerly used language of art, given the geopolitical positioning of a state troubled with war and insurgence. The dramatic demonstration became an announcement of an artistic breakthrough, as it were, comprising a breakaway from continuing modernist tradition, quest for inspiration in daily life practice, and use of the visual vernacular.


Emotional transformation associated with experiencing history and the varying paths of individual memory, coupled with changes brought by the Iraq War to daily life and the society are a major component of the exhibition. While developing a new language of art in a country ravaged by war and the social experience of struggling for economic survival is particularly difficult, it did produce a number of vital works and introduce a number of major characters to the art scene. Exhibition-related research spanned many years from the year 2007 onwards, i.a. thanks to workshops delivered in the Iraqi part of Kurdistan by Polish curator Aneta Szyłak and Hiwa K, an internationally renowned Kurdish artist residing in Berlin; the majority of artists showing their works at this exhibition were active participants of these workshops.

Artists invited to join the exhibition are in their thirties and forties; most have had the opportunity of studying abroad, chiefly in Germany, the United Kingdom, or Scandinavia. Some have returned and are teaching at art schools, while others remained in the diaspora. Invitees include the following, among others: Hiwa K (Berlin), Sherko Abbas (Manchester), Kani Kamil (Manchester), Shirwan Fatih (Sulaymaniyah), Rebeen Hamarafiq (Sulaymaniyah), Rozhgar Mustafa (Sulaymaniyah), Sakar Sleman (Sulaymaniyah), Walid Siti (London), Halgurd A. Baram (Sulaymaniyah).

The exhibition comprises a number of multimedia installations, sculptures, drawings and photographs, all of which will fill the space of Białystok’s Arsenal Gallery with multi-dimensional, emotional narrative carrying an extraordinary cultural and political message.

Aneta Szyłak

* We are using the name “Sulaymaniyah”. The official index of Polish geographical names published by the Head Office of Geodesy and Cartography (2019 edition) lists the city as As-Sulajmanijja; transcribed from the Arabic, it is considered offensive by the Kurds. The city’s name in Kurdish reads “Silêmanî”.

Translated by Aleksandra Sobczak-Kövesi

items.title: 2017, 2019 Running Around Cigarette Factory
items.summary: Running Around Cigarette Factory 2017, 2019. The work started when, at the beginning of the transformation of the old Cigarette Factory into the…
items.content_html:
Running Around Cigarette Factory 2017, 2019. The work started when, at the beginning of the transformation of the old Cigarette Factory into the new Culture Factory, many groups who were claiming and fighting for the place started to publish their project for the place in social media. In contrast, as the fight started to be directed toward social media, I prepared a participatory performance. I invited everyone to have a walk and a run around the factory, just to make it clear that the factory, 76,000 square metres in the middle of the city, is big enough to accommodate all activities in the city, not just a few groups. Mhamad Nakam, a young and interesting storyteller. wrote a short story, and the story was divided into 17 cards and spread across five places for the walkers to collect during the walk. By the end, because there were 17 cards and each person collected only 5, they had to share their card with others in order to re-make the story.

in 2019 the Material of the first performance was installed and made open to public and this time I invited audiences to re-invent part of a story written on 17 small carts.

items.title: Dropping Bucket and Objects
items.summary: 2017 Trilogy bucket leaking system. The installation involves four metal buckets: one is placed upside down on the floor, while the other three…
items.content_html:
2017 Trilogy bucket leaking system.

The installation involves four metal buckets: one is placed upside down on the floor, while the other three are suspended from the ceiling, stacked one atop the other. Each bucket has a hole that allows water to leak out. The last bucket is equipped with a tap underneath, which can be adjusted to control the dripping. The sound of the water drops hitting the upside-down bucket enhances the auditory experience of the installation.

Infinite Leaking Objects

The bucket had varied installations in different places and spaces, so installing the buckets opened up a variety of methods to play with, depending on the context.

items.title: Dropping: Canvas - Imago Mundi
items.summary: Imago Mundi, One Month, 10,000,000 drops of water leaked from the water system. For the project Imago Mundi, specifically for “Kurdistan - In-Between…
items.content_html:
Imago Mundi, One Month, 10,000,000 drops of water leaked from the water system.
For the project Imago Mundi, specifically for “Kurdistan - In-Between Worlds,” I was chosen as a contemporary Kurdish artist and provided with a 10x12cm canvas to create an artwork. I discovered several tanks in the city’s water system that were leaking, with drops of water coming from various locations. I positioned the canvas beneath one leak for one month, and by estimation, I calculated that around ten million drops struck the canvas at its centre during that time.

Catalogues: Kurdistan in between worlds.

items.title: BECOMING A DOG
items.summary: 2013 The process of the work started from a second-hand market near Goldsmith College when I bout an album for one pound; it…
items.content_html:
2013 The process of the work started from a second-hand market near Goldsmith College when I bout an album for one pound; it looked nice and old-style. My surprise was it was full of pictures, and when I asked about the pictures, they said it was free; you could throw it away. Then the Idea of turning this material that has zero value into an experience and a little discovery, and maybe give it value through making it into artwork that has value to others. The research happened when there was no AI to give the picture to and analyse the symbols; then I had to go through the pictures one by one, finding symbols and places that are possible to visit. The closest place I found in the picture was a castle called  Hampton Court Palace.

How to find the places name and when it located it needed many days of comparation between  pictures of palaces in UK to find the perfect match and while the the family had a visit to the side the two couple and a son aged between 15 to 20 probably, and a dog, I wanted to visit the site but while the visiting new places gives you exciting interest for new palace or things to see, this excitement all has gone through thousand pictures of the place of every corner, every inch. Then I thought seeing the place as a human who builds a very complicated system of images that kills the feeling of new experiences is not possible. 

I started thinking what the experience would be if I visited as a dog that was in the pictures. From this perspective, I attached a Handycam to my head and visited the place, walking on my knees and hands to position my head in the dog's place. The first show of the whole work as an installation was inside my studio for the visiting tutors. I filled a wall with pictures of the place, and the video I recorded with the camera also had to be edited to look like the dog's vision; the video had to become square, with the possibilities that dogs see 290 angles instead of humans' 180 angles and reduced to the colours the dog sees.  I tried to get as much out of the materials as possible, like I did a little animation to get the album ready for research and artwork, but it was never fully ready for exhibition on its own in London.

2017 The Workshop at Silemany University.

When the University of Silemani asked me to do a seminar in the College, I thought it would be better to do a workshop for students that motivates them to understand both the curating process and to build their own work from unknown materials that are new to them. After the materials were used to make their own exhibition. I gave my seminar on the day of the exhibition to show that there are various viewpoints for the same material.

items.title: Ladybug, ladybug, where is my uncle's house.
items.summary: Ladybug, ladybug, where is my uncle's house 2016 Ladybug, ladybug, where is my uncle's house. خاڵخاڵۆکە ماڵی خاڵم لە کوێیە The work is…
items.content_html:
2016 Ladybug, ladybug, where is my uncle's house.
خاڵخاڵۆکە ماڵی خاڵم لە کوێیە

The work is a performance or an action during the teachers' strike, while all the participants were shouting Where is our salary out loud. I started to repeatedly tell Ladybug, " Ladybug, where is my uncle's house.  ( خاڵخاڵۆکە ماڵی خاڵم لە کوێیە ) A Kurdish riddle made as an illusion for kids: when they capture the Ladybug, they will sing the riddle, and the illusion is that the Ladybug will travel in the direction of one's uncle's house. Even the original song's words build illusory, performative power leading to action. During this performance, even the song was sung for a plastic ladybug, which reduces performativity from the riddle completely.

Documentation; Rozhgar Mustafa.

items.title: Tunning Body
items.summary: 2016 Tunning body, performance staged for Camera, 18:18 minute. TUNNING BODY, 2016 “Tunning Body” shows tension between violence, dance and sound. While the…
items.content_html:
TUNNING BODY, 2016
“Tunning Body” shows tension between violence, dance and sound. While the sticks are a Kurdish musical instrument, shimshal, they are at the same time sticks used in martial arts. The body takes position among these complexities, reflecting the reality of Kurdish society in Iraq.
The work grew from an experiment with body and sound, devised for the project “Clamour” Curated By Sherko Abbas at the exhibition hall institute of fine art, Sulaimaniyah
The first time the work was shown was as a video documentation of the actual performance.

For the first time I did the performance live and in front of an audience for the project Space21. This opens up possibilities for many other directions in which the work can develop. Simultaneously, it records layers of politics and history embedded in different locations.
